EMPLOYMENT CONTRACT

between
Ahornweid Trading Ltd, Basel, represented by Eva Vogel, Managing Director (employer)
and
Jack Foster, Kirchgasse 77, 4051 Basel (employee)

1. Position
Warehouse supervisor, full-time, shift work including night shifts.

2. Supplements
For work between 23:00 and 06:00 a supplement of 25% of the hourly wage is paid.

3. Working hours
42 hours per week according to the shift plan.

attachments.text:
From: Jack Foster
To: Eva Vogel, Ahornweid Trading Ltd
Subject: Night supplement not paid

Dear Ms Vogel

According to my contract I am entitled to a 25% supplement for night work. This supplement has not been paid for my night shifts in the last months. By my calculation the outstanding amount is CHF 575. I ask you to pay this amount with my next salary.

Kind regards
Jack Foster

---

From: Eva Vogel
To: Jack Foster
Subject: RE: Night supplement not paid

Mr Foster, we will look at this. I would ask you not to raise such matters in front of the team.
E. Vogel

questions.label: Q1
questions.question: Did the employee ask the employer to state the reasons for the notice in writing?

questions.label: Q2
questions.question: Did the employee lodge a written objection to the notice with the employer (German: "beim Kündigenden schriftlich Einsprache erheben") no later than the end of the notice period?

questions.label: Q3
questions.question: Did the employer give the employee notice of termination of the employment relationship?

questions.label: Q4
questions.question: Did the employee and the employer agree, after the notice, that the employment relationship would continue?

questions.label: Q5
questions.question: Have more than 180 days passed since the employment relationship ended?

questions.label: Q6
questions.question: Did the employee make the compensation claim pending (German: "Klage anhängig gemacht") within 180 days of the end of the employment relationship?

questions.label: Q7
questions.question: Was the notice given because the employee had asserted, in good faith, claims arising from the employment relationship?

questions.label: Q8
questions.question: Was the employee, when notice was given, an elected employee representative on the staff council of the business or on a body linked to the business?

questions.label: Q9
questions.question: Has the notice period (from the notice to the end of the employment relationship) already ended?

text:
Dear Sir or Madam,

A few days after I was given notice, I wrote to Eva Vogel, the head of Ahornweid Trading Ltd in Basel, and asked her to give me the reasons for the notice in writing. I'm still waiting for anything meaningful.

I'm attaching the e-mails in which I asked the company for the money I'm owed, together with the reply I got, and the first page of my employment contract.

The notice came on 11 May 2026. Ms Vogel called me into her office and gave me a letter ending my employment.

I'm still employed there at the moment, so my job hasn't actually ended yet, let alone half a year ago.

To answer a question my sister asked: I'm not on any staff committee or workers' body at the company. I'm a warehouse supervisor, nothing more.

Why do I think I was let go? Because I asked for what I'm due. For months I worked night shifts without the night supplement that's in my contract, CHF 575 in total. I put that in writing, I was sure I was in the right, and I still am. Ms Vogel was clearly annoyed, and my colleague Tara Bucher heard her say that 'people who come with lists of demands can look for work elsewhere'. Not long after, I had my notice.

I've also attached my pay slip for June.

My notice period hasn't run out yet: it ends on 31 July, and until then I'm still going in to work every day.

What can I do about this, and is it worth it?

Yours faithfully,
Jack Foster
Kirchgasse 77, Basel
